thread:
marie chen: Hey team — baby born overseas while I was on parental leave (yay!). Need to add newborn to medical + dental + HSA/FSA. A few Qs: 1) what evidence do you accept for a foreign birth (we got a Consular Report of Birth Abroad and a local birth cert)? 2) SSN: can I enroll now and provide SSN later, or does carrier need it up front? 3) can coverage be effective retro to birth date, and how does payroll proration/retro deduction work? 4) if I switch HSA to family midyear, how will contributions be prorated vs IRS limits? Thanks! :baby_bottle:

olivia (People Ops): Huge congrats @marie! Short answers: 1) we accept CRBA (Consular Report of Birth Abroad), the foreign birth certificate (with certified English translation), AND the child's passport. Please upload PDFs to the dependent add portal: https://benefits.redwood.com/forms/dependent-add — choose "Newborn" as QLE reason. 2) You can enroll the child without SSN right away, carriers typically allow pending enrollment; however you must provide the SSN within 60 days of enrollment (carrier requirement). If carrier needs it sooner we'll reach out. 3) Coverage can be effective retro to the birth date if you request within the 30-day QLE window. Payroll will prorate deductions starting from the coverage effective date; if that date is before the most recent paycheck we will process a retro payroll adjustment on the next run to capture missed premiums. If effective date falls mid-pay-period we'll compute per‑paycheck prorate. 4) HSA: you can change your HSA election as a QLE. Payroll will prorate contributions for the remainder of the year; note annual IRS contribution limits still apply, so your remaining contribution allowance is pro-rated. Recommend confirming with payroll if you expect to max the HSA so we can avoid excess withholding. :memo:

people-ops-bot: Reminder: 30-day QLE window for newborns. SSN must be provided within 60 days when required by carrier. Upload docs here: https://benefits.redwood.com/forms/dependent-add :information_source:

ben (Benefits): Adding a note on carrier timing — when evidence is foreign-language or CRBA, carriers can take longer to process (usually 7-21 business days). Enroll immediately so coverage is recorded; carrier will issue member IDs once SSN is received or processing completes. Dental is a separate election but uses the same dependent add workflow. Dependent Care FSA substantiation is separate from medical enrollment (if you're using dependent care FSA, you'll need receipts/claims to be eligible). For HSA limits: if you move from single to family midyear, the IRS max is determined by months of family coverage — we and payroll will help calculate the allowed contribution. DM payroll or Ben if you want a quick projection.

marie chen: Thanks — uploaded CRBA + passport to portal and selected "Newborn". Also quick Q: do pediatricians need immunization records to accept the plan or for assigning a PCP? (we're setting up first appointments in a couple weeks)

olivia (People Ops): Good call — carriers don't require immunization records to enroll. Pediatricians may request records for well-child visits or school. If the pediatrician's office asks for proof of coverage or member ID and you don't yet have it, send them the temporary coverage confirmation PDF after you enroll or show the portal submission screenshot. We'll follow up here if a carrier asks for additional docs. :white_check_mark:

marie chen: Awesome, thanks everyone — appreciate the fast help! I'll DM if carrier asks for anything else. :heart:
